test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 8 Mar 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT a source of the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Constitution of Denmark**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian Constitution has borrowed several features from various other constitutions of the world to create a comprehensive document.
 
• From the **Constitution of Ireland**, we adopted the Directive Principles of State Policy.
 
• The **Constitution of France** influenced the ideals of Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity which are enshrined in the Preamble.
 
• The **Constitution of the U.S.A** provided the framework for the Fundamental Rights, the federal structure of government, and the independence of the judiciary.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitution of Ireland**

 
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution were borrowed from the Irish Constitution.
 
• These principles provide guidelines for the creation of a just society in India and are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• They are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by any court, but they are fundamental in the governance of the country and aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
 
 
• **Constitution of France**
 
 
• The ideals of Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity were taken from the French Constitution and are included in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These principles were inspired by the French Revolution and emphasize the importance of individual freedom, equality before the law, and brotherhood among people.
 
 
 
• **Constitution of the U.S.A**
 
 
• The Indian Constitution borrowed the concept of Fundamental Rights from the U.S. Constitution.
 
• The structure of federalism, with a clear demarcation of powers between the central and state governments, was also adopted from the U.S. model.
 
• The idea of an independent judiciary, with the power of judicial review, was another significant feature borrowed from the U.S. Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Constitution of Denmark**
 
 
• The Constitution of Denmark has not been a direct source for any specific part of the Indian Constitution.
 
• While the Indian Constitution is influenced by various global constitutions, Denmark's constitution does not have a direct influence on the Indian legal framework.
